title: Vegetable Gratin
description: This dish from Quick Cuisine International – French, is very similar to a classic Tian. It is both a vessel and the name of what’s cooked in it: summer vegetables, sliced quite thin, arranged in careful layers, drenched in quality olive oil and then cooked in a slow oven until each individual vegetable surrenders to the others, becoming one. The true and complete melding of earthy zucchini, sweet onion, waxy potato, juicy and acidic tomatoes is the great achievement of a well-made Tian. This one from Quick Cuisine is a very easy preparation (and with cheese!): “One of my most popular side dishes.”
ingredients: 2 long baking potatoes, sliced very thinly
½ cup of so of breadcrumbs (optional)
directions: Heat garlic in olive oil for about 5 minutes. (This may be done in advance.)

In a shallow 9 x 13 oval baking dish, arrange vegetables in alternating layers, starting with half of each: potatoes, onions (optional), zucchini, tomatoes, and cheese, then sprinkling some fine herbs and salt and pepper. Repeat.
Sprinkle with garlic oil and bake for about 45 minutes. (Optionally, you could sprinkle on some breadcrumbs and spritz with a little olive oil.)
Meanwhile, stack and roll the basil leaves, then slice thinly in shreds (chiffonade).
When vegetables are tender, remove from over and sprinkle with shredded basil.
Serve hot or at room temperature.
